description:
About the Position

Maynooth University invites applications for a 36-month postdoctoral researcher position on the BIOCHAR project, focused on life cycle assessment of biochar systems. The researcher will quantify the environmental and climate performance of biochar production and application pathways, from feedstock sourcing and pyrolysis to field application, using established LCA methods and Irish and European datasets. The post is funded at EUR 44,273 per annum on a fixed-term contract and sits within the university's expanding research portfolio on sustainable bioresources and the circular economy.

Biochar is increasingly promoted as a negative-emissions and soil-improvement technology, but credible climate accounting depends on rigorous assessment of the full production and use chain. The postdoctoral researcher will build and refine life cycle models, work with project partners on primary data collection, and translate results into peer-reviewed publications and policy-relevant outputs. The role offers experience across LCA software, uncertainty analysis and interaction with agronomy and engineering colleagues.

Candidate Profile and Environment

Applicants hold a PhD in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry, process engineering or a closely related discipline, with demonstrable experience in life cycle assessment or comparable environmental systems analysis. Familiarity with carbon accounting, agricultural systems or negative-emissions technologies is an advantage. The postdoctoral researcher joins an active research group at Maynooth with links to Irish and European biochar and bioeconomy networks, and the project timeline supports conference participation and international collaboration.

Highlights

  • 36-month fixed-term postdoctoral contract
  • EUR 44,273 per annum salary
  • Life cycle assessment of biochar production and use pathways
  • Carbon accounting and negative-emissions technologies
  • Peer-reviewed publication and policy-relevant outputs
  • Collaboration across agronomy, engineering and climate research

It combines a strong research profile in the sciences, social sciences, humanities, engineering and education with close student-faculty ratios. The university hosts funded research centres across climate, smart technologies, social science and health, and its postdoctoral researchers work on nationally and internationally funded projects, including EU Horizon and Science Foundation Ireland programmes.
